hints: Simplify the algebraic fraction to get $5x$.
Evaluate the range using the given domain $x \ge 0$.
walkthrough:
Simplify the compound fraction by multiplying the numerator and denominator by $(5x + 2)$:
$$fg(x) = \frac{4(5x + 2) - 8}{4} = \frac{20x + 8 - 8}{4} = \frac{20x}{4} = 5x$$

Determine the range of $fg(x)$ based on the domain $x \ge 0$:
$$\text{Since } x \ge 0 \implies fg(x) = 5x \ge 0 \implies \text{Range is } y \ge 0 \quad (\text{or } fg(x) \ge 0)$$

hints: Find the range of $g(x)$ when $x \ge 0$ to get the domain of $g^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Set $y = g(x)$ and rearrange to make $x$ the subject:
$$y = \frac{4}{5x + 2} \implies 5x + 2 = \frac{4}{y} \implies 5x = \frac{4}{y} - 2 = \frac{4 - 2y}{y}$$

Write the inverse function in terms of $x$:
$$g^{-1}(x) = \frac{4 - 2x}{5x}$$

Determine the domain of $g^{-1}(x)$, which is the range of $g(x)$ for $x \ge 0$:
$$\text{At } x = 0:\quad g(0) = \frac{4}{2} = 2; \quad \text{as } x \to \infty, \quad g(x) \to 0$$
$$\text{Domain of } g^{-1} \text{ is } 0 < x \le 2$$
